page: Microsoft Azure DC64as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AMD EPYC 9V74 processors hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V. It allocates 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. System memory measures 256 GB, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The x86_64 CPU configuration enables hardware cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as standard AVX vector support, while omitting AVX-512 extensions and discrete graphics acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate notable multi-threaded scaling. In stress-ng execution, the instance achieves an average single-core score of 1,993.66, whereas its multi-core score reaches 68,550.78, placing it in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Caching benchmarks with Redis SET operations record an average throughput of 57.65 million operations per second. A key architectural characteristic is the complete absence of local instance storage, requiring instances to rely on remote persistent block storage. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the DC64as_v5 provides high core density per virtual machine, balancing substantial CPU resources with standard memory capacity without the added cost overhead of local NVMe drives or specialized accelerator hardware. This balance of 64 dedicated execution threads and strong parallel throughput aligns with enterprise application hosting, batch ETL pipelines, distributed software compilation, and containerized microservice platforms.
description: Microsoft Azure DC64as_v5 is a general-purpose instance providing 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256 GB of memory, built on 32 physical cores of AMD EPYC 9V74 processors running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provides a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation alongside hardware cryptography instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. In synthetic benchmarking, the instance achieves average single-core performance in stress-ng at 1,993.66 but delivers top-quartile multi-core throughput at 68,550.78, accompanied by 57.65 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. Because the configuration includes no local storage, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no GPU hardware, operational designs depend on external networking and remote storage. This resource density supports parallel batch computing, continuous integration pipelines, and scaled microservices.
